## Attack description

An adversary tries every possible value for a password until they succeed. A brute force attack, if feasible computationally, will always be successful because it will essentially go through all possible passwords given the alphabet used (lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, symbols, etc.) and the maximum length of the password.

rounds.answer:
The knowledge base outlines several consequences of password cracking, particularly through brute force attacks. These include:

1. **Access to Valid Accounts**: Adversaries may successfully gain access to accounts by brute forcing passwords, especially when they have gathered information from other post-compromise behaviors like credential dumping or account discovery [Source 1].

2. **Systematic Guessing**: When passwords are unknown, adversaries can systematically guess them using brute force techniques, which can be executed through interactions with services that validate credentials [Source 3].

3. **Computational Feasibility**: Brute force attacks, if computationally feasible, will eventually succeed as they attempt every possible password combination based on the character set and maximum password length [Source 2].

These consequences highlight the risks associated with weak password policies and the importance of implementing strong authentication measures.
